place.zh: 沉鼎山 · 后山崖顶 · 九月初三
place.en: Mount Chending · The clifftop · The third of the ninth month

setup.zh: 九月初三，天是晴的。师父一早下山扫台阶去了。你在草屋前的青石上盘腿坐下，胸口揣着那颗九转筑基丹。
setup.en: The third of the ninth month, a clear day. Your master went down at dawn to sweep the steps. You sit cross-legged on the bluestone before the hut, the nine-turn Foundation pill against your chest.

recap.zh: 九月初三，崖顶上扣着一团锅盖云——你筑基了。师父问「几道纹？」，你说「一道」。他说：「你外公那一步，你替他走完了。」
recap.en: On the third of the ninth month a pot-lid cloud sat over the clifftop — you laid your Foundation. Your master asked, "How many rings?" You said, "One." He said: "The step your grandfather never finished — you have finished it for him."

zh: 师父在山下，扫同一级台阶。
en: The third of the ninth month, a clear day.
Down below, your master sweeps one step, over and over.
Grandfather, this step I take for you.

story.zh:
可外公呢？外公手里捏的，是一颗一转、下品、带着黑斑的丹，身后站着的，是一个说「吃」的师父。外公冲不过，还能下山，教娃娃算账；他冲不过，这辈子便只有一双练气的腿，泗水渡口那个人，在山门外头等着。

小满先掐了一撮鼎苔嚼了，满嘴的土腥气，又把那颗九转筑基丹放进嘴里。他没有先嚼，含了一会儿，心里说：外公，这一步，我替你走。说完了，才咽下去。
story.en:
And Grandfather? What Grandfather had held was a one-turn, low-grade, dark-flecked pill, and behind him stood a master who said "eat". If Grandfather failed, he could still go down the mountain and teach children their sums; if Xiaoman failed, he would have nothing all his life but a pair of Qi Refining legs, and the man at the Si ferry was waiting outside the gate.

Xiaoman first pinched off some cauldron moss and chewed it, a mouthful of the taste of earth, then put the nine-turn Foundation pill in his mouth. He did not bite it at once; he held it a while and said in his heart: Grandfather, this step I take for you. Only when he had said it did he swallow.

exits.means: swallows the pill and pushes through to the Foundation, attempts the breakthrough

refuse.zh: 丹田那片湖还没满。九层圆满之前，冲不得——先回去，把功课做满。
refuse.en: The lake in your dantian is not full yet. Before layer nine, Consummation, you cannot push — go back and fill your practice first.

story.zh:
正疑惑间，天忽然暗了下来。他抬头一看，头顶上不知何时聚起了一团云。那云不大，只罩着这一座崖顶，灰里透白，慢慢地转，越转越快，竟转成了一口倒扣的大锅。四下里的风一齐停了，松树不响了，鸟不叫了，连崖下那道瀑布的水声，都像隔了一层棉被。云心里透下一缕光来，不偏不倚，正照在他头顶上。

就是这一晃。丹田里不知从哪里起了雾，一层一层漫上来，漫过了那座台子，台子在雾里晃。他看见一扇门。

门上贴着一张纸，纸上写着几个字，他一个也看不清，只觉得那几个字，写的一定是「勿入」。

跑吧。他心里有个声音说。那声音说得很轻，很有道理：收了功，散了灵力，停在练气，也能活，也能回家，教娃娃算账。跑不丢人，娘说的。

他没去跟那个声音争。他只做了一样最旧的事，学吐纳头一个冬天便会了的：把胸口那口憋住的气，像娘蹲在灶前吹那几块炭，细细地、长长地吐出去，吐得比吸进来的长。心口跳得像风里的灯苗，这一口吐下去，灯苗矮了一矮，不那么乱扑了。怕还在，台子也还在晃；可那个声音，不再是他心里唯一的声音了。

雾却没散，雾里又浮出一扇门来。这一扇他认得：门框是爹砍的松木，门轴装歪了，开关都得往上抬一抬——石坳村，他自己家的门，西山梁上他看着他爹抬了一下、关上的那一扇。门外头一片雪地，雪地里站着一个人，一身白衣，背着手，一动也不动，往门里看——那年冬天跟着马三挨家挨户站一站的，就是这个样子。镜子那头的人，知道他是哪里来的。

他差一点又信了它。可他一口气吐到底，便看明白了：停在练气回了家，那个人还站在门外头。一个练气的挡不住他，一个教娃娃算账的，更挡不住。到那时候，门里头不过多了一个挡不住人的人。

可便在这时，他想起了另一扇门。那是他爹说过的一扇门。他爹年轻的时候，给他外公的私塾送一只野兔，门上贴着一张字，他爹不认得，怕写的是「闲人勿入」，就在门口站了一个时辰。站了一个时辰，他爹还是进去了。后来他娘说：「写的是『今日放学』。」小满在疼里头，竟笑了一下。

他爹不识字，站了一个时辰，还是进去了。他娘识字，嫁给了一个站了一个时辰才敢进门的人。他外公的门，原来他爹早就进过了；门上写的，也从来不是「勿入」。一个人怕，原不是不进门的道理。

他不跑了。他往那座晃着的台子上，又夯了一下。

丹田里的雾，一丝一丝地散了。台子顶上，头一回有了天，天上淡淡的，亮着几颗星。

原来这便是**筑基**。台子落定的那一刻，头顶那口「锅」悄没声地散了。云开处，星星比平日亮了一些，近了一些。

瞿老道：「几道纹？」

小满道：「……一道。」瞿老没有说话。他看他的脸，看他的眼睛，看他站在那里的样子——腿稳，一点也不晃，脸上一个黑斑也没有，比进山门那天还干净。他当然看得出来。

可他只是点了点头，道：「嗯。一道。」然后他站起身来，走到崖边，背对着小满，望着山下那一片黑沉沉的石阶。望了很久，他道：

「你外公那一步，你替他走完了。」

阿禾最后一个来。她站在内门东头第三间的门口，没进门，隔着门槛看他，从头看到脚，看他那张脸——一个黑点也没有。她看了一会儿，道：「观里那颗？」小满道：「观里那颗。」阿禾点点头，掏出小本子记了一笔，合上，道：「我不问。这一行，不算利息。」说完便走了。
story.en:
Just as he began to wonder, the sky suddenly darkened.

He looked up: at some moment a cloud had gathered overhead. It was not large — it covered only this one clifftop, grey going white — turning slowly, then faster and faster, until it was a great upturned pot.

It was that one sway. In his dantian a fog rose from nowhere, layer on layer, until it covered the platform, and the platform swayed in it. He saw a door.

On the door was pasted a sheet of paper with a few words on it; he could not make out one of them, but he felt sure the words must say "Do not enter".

Run, said a voice in his heart.

He did not argue with the voice. He did only the oldest thing he knew, learned in his first winter of breathing: he let the breath held in his chest go out thin and long, the way his mother blew on the embers in the stove, longer out than in. His heart had been leaping like a flame in the wind; with that one breath the flame ducked lower and stopped flailing. The fear was still there, and the platform still swayed; but that voice was no longer the only voice in him.

But the mist did not clear, and out of it rose another door. This one he knew: the frame was pine his father had cut, the hinge set crooked so you had to lift it to open or shut — Shi'ao village, his own door, the one he had watched his father lift and shut from the West Ridge. Outside it lay snow, and in the snow stood a man in white, hands behind his back, not moving, looking in at the door — just as he had stood a moment at every door that winter, behind Ma San. The man at the other end of the mirror knew where he came from.

He nearly believed the voice again. But he breathed all the way out, and saw it plainly: stop at Qi Condensation and go home, and that man would still be standing outside the door. A Qi Condensation man could not stop him; a man teaching children their sums, still less. And then there would only be one more person inside the door who could stop no one.

But just then, he remembered another door.

His father could not read, stood there for an hour, and went in all the same. His mother could read, and married a man who had stood an hour before daring to go through a door. His grandfather's door — his father had gone through it long ago; and what was written on it had never been "Do not enter". Being afraid was never a reason not to go through a door.

He did not run. He pounded the swaying platform down once more.

The fog in his dantian thinned, strand by strand. Above the platform, for the first time, there was a sky, and in it, faintly, a few stars.

So this was the **Foundation**.

The moment the platform settled, the "pot" overhead thinned away without a sound. Where the cloud opened, the stars were a little brighter than usual, a little nearer.

Old Qu said: "How many rings?"

Xiaoman said: "…One."

But he only nodded and said: "Mm. One."

"The step your grandfather never finished — you have finished it for him."

A He came last. She stood at the door of the third room at the east end of the inner court, didn't come in, looked at him across the threshold from head to foot, looked at his face — not one dark fleck on it. She looked a while, and said: "The temple's one?" Xiaoman said: "The temple's one."

A He nodded, took out her little notebook, made a note, shut it, and said: "I'm not asking. This line isn't interest." Then she left.

exits.means: wants to stop, run, or wait before the breakthrough

text.zh: 你想起师父那一句：进了一半想退，那一剑，自己先散了。
text.en: You remember your master's words: half-way in and wanting to back out, the sword falls apart on its own.
